report:
Reviewed the complete rooted_equality claim, both ordinary implementation associations, and all eight ordinary associated tests. No TODO or N/A entries exist. Requirements are rooted semantic equality and deterministic structural fingerprints driving equality, ordering, hashing, and Salsa updates, independent of stash addresses, allocation order, padding, and unreachable entries.

Implementation inspection: Stashed::new starts FingerprintHasher at the supplied root, rather than hashing the stash buffer. The immutable stored fingerprint alone drives PartialEq/Eq, Hash, Ord, and PartialOrd; Salsa Update compares Stashed equality and retains equal old values, replacing differing values. FingerprintHasher initializes Xxh3 deterministically and hashes pointer referents recursively; slices include length and elements in logical order. Its entry-index cache memoizes fingerprints without feeding indices or addresses into the digest. Thus unreachable entries and different allocation layouts cannot contribute. The associated macro file generates field-by-field hashing for named/tuple structs and variants, with enum variant tags; it never hashes raw struct storage, so padding does not contribute. Primitive/direct and Option hashing and all storage/fingerprint helpers are in the associated complete lib.rs file. Essential implementation files are already associated.

Tests: fingerprint_deterministic constructs identical values in separate stashes and asserts equality. stashed_eq_compound_dag checks recursive Option/Ptr structure with a shared leaf. stashed_hash_consistent_with_eq verifies equal content has equal output hashes; stashed_ne_different_content_fingerprint verifies changed fields are unequal; stashed_ord_consistent_with_eq asserts Equal ordering. reachable_content_controls_equality_hash_and_order covers all combinations of reversed allocation order and unreachable allocations before/after the root, asserting equality, identical hashes, equal ordering, changed-content inequality, non-equal ordering, reverse-order symmetry, and stable ordering against the changed semantic value. Captured tree setup uses a slice root [a,b,a] with padded referents, exercising pointer and slice traversal and repeated cached children. padded_values_fingerprint_only_semantic_fields proves actual padding exists and compares the derived fingerprint to explicitly hashing only the two semantic fields. salsa_update_keeps_equal_root_and_replaces_changed_root verifies false/retention for equal content with changed allocation layout, true/replacement for changed content, and reads the new reachable value 21. Captured Point, Padded, tree, and hash helper context establishes the fixtures and assertions. A regression to hashing pointer indices, entire allocations, or raw padded bytes would be detected by these tests; incorrect update decisions and ordering/hashing inconsistency are directly asserted.

Execution: ran cargo test -p sage-stash --features salsa --test storage_contracts --test arena_tests successfully: 46 arena tests and 10 storage-contract tests passed, including all eight associated tests and the feature-gated Salsa test. This execution supplements the implementation/test adequacy review. No Rust source changes were made. No edits requested.
